definitions.explanation: The act of being forced to leave a building or land, typically by legal or official order.

examples.japanese: {立|た}ち{退|の}きを{命|めい}じられた。
{住民|じゅうみん}は{立|た}ち{退|の}きに{反対|はんたい}している。
examples.english: The residents are opposing the eviction.

examples.japanese: {再開発|さいかいはつ}のため、このビルの{住民|じゅうみん}は{来月|らいげつ}までに{立|た}ち{退|の}きを{求|もと}められている。
examples.english: Due to redevelopment, the residents of this building are being asked to vacate by next month.

notes:
Derived from the verb {立|た}ち{退|の}く (to vacate, to move out). Used in legal and real estate contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {立|た}ち{退|の}きを{命|めい}じる: to order an eviction
- {立|た}ち{退|の}きを{求|もと}める: to demand eviction
- {立|た}ち{退|の}き{料|りょう}: eviction compensation money
- {立|た}ち{退|の}き{要求|ようきゅう}: eviction demand
- {強制|きょうせい}{立|た}ち{退|の}き: forced eviction

USAGE:
Often appears in news about urban redevelopment, landlord-tenant disputes, and disaster evacuations. In Japan, tenants have strong legal protections, so {立|た}ち{退|の}き often involves negotiation over {立|た}ち{退|の}き{料|りょう} (compensation).

RELATED WORDS:
- {退去|たいきょ}: departure, vacating (more formal/neutral)
- {追|お}い{出|だ}す: to drive out, to kick out (more forceful)

cross_references.label: to drive out, to kick out
